headline: Keytruda patent expiry creates incentive for Merck to maximise profits from the Moderna combination before exclusivity ends
reasoning: Mirchandani notes that the Moderna-Merck partnership is a 50/50 profit split, and that Keytruda has been both highly successful and highly effective. With Keytruda's patent coming off in the near term, Merck has a strong incentive to extract as much value as possible from the combination therapy before exclusivity lapses. He views the partnership arrangement as adding another layer of complexity for investors but does not see the profit-sharing structure changing.

headline: Keytruda combination with Moderna's mRNA vaccine drove phase three melanoma trial success, reinforcing Merck's position as a key partner in expanding personalised cancer immunotherapy
reasoning: Mirchandani notes that Merck's Keytruda, described as an 'incredibly successful and effective drug' in treating melanoma and other cancers, was the combination partner in Moderna's phase three trial. The success of the combined approach validates both companies' technologies and underpins the commercial pathway for the melanoma indication. While his focus is on Moderna as the platform play, the partnership with Merck and Keytruda is presented as a key enabler of the trial's success.

headline: Personalised mRNA cancer therapy validated as a platform, with bladder and pancreatic pipeline representing larger addressable markets than melanoma alone
reasoning: Mirchandani frames the melanoma phase three result as proof-of-concept for personalised mRNA-based cancer therapy as a broader platform, not a single-product story. He argues the market has historically undervalued this approach because biotech R&D cycles are long and investor patience is limited. With results pending in bladder and pancreatic cancers — both of which affect more patients globally than melanoma — he sees the addressable market expanding significantly. Australia's melanoma incidence running at roughly nine times the global average also highlights near-term commercial relevance in the domestic market.
quote: Those cancers are much bigger. They're more more, um, individuals who are affected by those cancers. And so if we think about the opportunity for Moderna, um, the number of patients is going to be much, much bigger, um, in the future. So yes, the stock price has appreciated, albeit from a very depressed level. Um, they continue to invest in R&D. And so our views that the revenues and the opportunities are going to [grow].

headline: Bullish on mRNA platform value beyond Covid and melanoma, with bladder and pancreatic cancer pipeline representing a much larger patient opportunity than current valuation reflects
reasoning: Mirchandani views Moderna as a platform company whose mRNA technology is applicable across multiple cancer types and diseases, not just Covid vaccines or melanoma. The stock had fallen sharply from its Covid peak to around a $20 billion market cap, reflecting widespread skepticism before the phase three melanoma trial result (combining Moderna's technology with Merck's Keytruda) triggered a near-tripling in a single session. He notes much of the initial spike was likely short-covering from a heavily shorted position, meaning the underlying opportunity may not yet be fully priced in. The pipeline extends to bladder and pancreatic cancers, which have larger patient populations than melanoma, implying materially larger revenue opportunity over time. He acknowledges biotech R&D is expensive and slow, requiring patient capital, but believes the platform value will continue to be realised as trials succeed.
